newsitem.title: JAPAN: Low prices makes Yokohama Rubber trim forecast.
newsitem.headline: Low prices makes Yokohama Rubber trim forecast.

text.p: Low prices for replacement tyres forced Yokohama Rubber Co, Japan's number-two tyre maker, to trim its forecasts for sales and profit for 1996/97, company president Seiji Hagiwara said on Thursday.

Although the company expects record output in this business year ending March 31 and is enjoying strong exports, he said it lowered its forecast for 1996/97 group current profit to 6.5 billion yen from its May estimate of 9.0 billion yen.
Its group sales forecast for the year were also lowered slightly to 390 billion yen from the previous 400 billion yen.
The company's sales and profit are also under pressure from stiffer competition in the U.S. market, Hagiwara said.
Nevertheless, the company expects its tyre production to rise to a record 210,000 tonnes in 1996/97 from the previous year's 200,000 tonnes.

Yokohama Rubber said earlier that parent current profit in the half-year through September rose to 5.95 billion yen from 4.52 billion yen in the year-ago period. Hagiwara said this increase was fuelled by good export demand and strength in Japan's construction sector.
"Demand for tyres for export, especially to Asian and Middle Eastern countries, was good, fuelled by the yen's weakening trend against the dollar and the global trend of rising tyre demand," he said.
Exported tyres, which account for 30 percent of the tyre division's sales, posted a year-on-year gain of about 12 percent in April-September.

But overall sales in the company's tyre division, which accounted for 72.4 percent of total revenues, were off 0.6 percent from the same period a year ago at 89.59 billion yen. -- Tokyo Commodity Desk +81-3 3432 7431
